tasks.title: Eliminate the blocked-delete data-loss window with a cross-tab write lock

tasks.scopeChange: web/lib/sync/store.ts moved from read-only to owned by Ken on 2026-08-13 so the writers can take the lock. This is the whole point of the successor task.
acceptanceCriteria: A write committed in a second tab AFTER the pending-queue check, while a deleteDB is blocked and queued, is never destroyed: either the delete cannot remain armed, or writers cannot commit while a clear is in progress.

The fix is taken by the writers (navigator.locks in lib/sync/store.ts and/or an idb blocking/versionchange handler that closes other connections), not only by the clear path; a lock taken solely in clear.ts is explicitly insufficient.

A regression test seeds the write AFTER the queue check while the delete is blocked, and fails against 2ec3457; the prior test only covered a write seeded before the check, which is why 68/68 passed while the bug was live.
After any interleaving that loses or could lose writing, the UI never renders a verified-clear claim; if the app cannot prove the device is clean it must say so.
The clear-device guidance no longer instructs the user to take an action that destroys data.

Every previously passing acceptance criterion of P0UI-001 still holds, and no existing test is weakened or deleted.

tasks.title: Phase 1: v2 sync contracts and the one-write-path rule
tasks.objective: BUILD_PLAN tenet 7 and section 3.4: sync push must be the SOLE browser mutation path for learner entities, and v2 resource routes are read-only. Today SyncEntity in the frozen v1 contract covers only entry/thread/person/progress/log/stage; the six v2 entities have no sync representation at all. This task adds the v2 sync contract and its validation, and enforces the one-write-path rule at the API layer. It deliberately does NOT wire persistence into lib/db/sync.ts - that follows once this contract is agreed, so the two can be reviewed separately.
acceptanceCriteria: A v2 sync entity vocabulary covers the six new entities (session, claim, motif, connection, application, teachingDraft) as a runtime const array plus derived type, in a NEW versioned module. web/lib/contracts.ts stays byte-stable and its v1 SyncEntity is NOT modified.
Zod schemas validate a v2 push payload for every one of those entities, reusing the enum arrays exported by lib/contracts/study-v2.ts rather than retyping any string literal.

Every v2 op carries the fields master plan section 14 names: opId, deviceId, entity, entityId, mutation, baseRevision, mutationGroupId, dependsOn, payload, clientTime. Validation rejects a payload missing any required field.

The revision cross-check is fail-closed by default in the same spirit as the v1 fix in SYNC-001: an op whose payload timestamp does not match its envelope is rejected, and the accessor pattern that fix introduced is followed rather than hardcoding one field name.

A related-creation group (session plus its claims plus their evidence) is expressible as a bounded atomic group via mutationGroupId, with dependsOn available for the cases where atomicity is not possible. Test that a group with a dangling dependsOn reference is rejected.

The one-write-path rule is expressed as an enforceable, tested predicate - not prose. Provide a function or type-level guard making it explicit that v2 resource routes are read-only and mutations go through sync push, and test that a mutation-shaped request against a read-only v2 route shape is rejected.
NO persistence in this task: lib/db/sync.ts and db/schema.ts are read-only here. Say plainly in the report that persistence wiring is deliberately deferred.

tasks.title: Prove the devotional/theology trigger against a real Postgres engine
tasks.objective: SCHEMAFU-001 implemented the cross-table devotional/theology rule as a deferrable constraint trigger in migration 0007, but proved it only by asserting on generated SQL text plus a pure-JS truth table over the extracted guard condition. That is honest and it is not nothing - but it does not prove Postgres actually rejects the violating write. This repo already has the right harness for that: web/tests/db-invariants.sql proves migration 0003 own triggers with real fixtures against a disposable database. Extend it.
acceptanceCriteria: db-invariants.sql gains fixtures proving all THREE new constraint triggers reject their violating write at the engine level: citing a devotional connection as evidence for a theology claim; relabeling an already-cited connection to devotional under a theology claim; retyping a claim to theology while it already cites devotional evidence.

Each fixture also proves the ALLOWED cases still pass - a devotional connection cited for a NON-theology claim, and a non-devotional connection cited for a theology claim - so the trigger is shown to be discriminating rather than blanket-rejecting.

The deferrable behaviour is exercised: a single transaction that temporarily violates the invariant mid-way but satisfies it by COMMIT must succeed, since that is the entire reason the trigger is DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED rather than immediate.
Follow the file existing style and structure for migration 0003 fixtures exactly; do not restructure what is already there.

If no Postgres is reachable in the run environment, DO NOT fake it or claim it passed - state plainly that the SQL is written but unexecuted, and say exactly how a human would run it (the command and what a pass looks like).

tasks.title: Resolve whether claim_evidence and motif_sightings need sync entities
tasks.objective: SYNCV2-001 surfaced a genuine documentation gap instead of silently choosing. THEOLOGY_MASTER_BUILD_PLAN section 14 prose describes related-creation groups covering session, claim, EVIDENCE, motif and connection - and BUILD_PLAN section 3.4 literal list names only six entities (session, claim, motif, connection, application, teachingDraft), omitting claim_evidence and motif_sightings. Both omitted things are real tables with real rows that a second device would need. Either they sync as their own entities, or they sync as part of a parent aggregate - but the docs must say which, because the wire format is being frozen right now.
acceptanceCriteria: Both documents state explicitly and identically whether claim_evidence and motif_sightings are (a) their own sync entities, or (b) carried as ordered children inside a parent aggregate push. No ambiguity, no silence.
Whichever is chosen, the contract and Zod schemas in sync-v2 match it, and a test proves a payload of the NOT-chosen shape is rejected - so the decision is enforced rather than merely documented.
If the aggregate option is chosen, the atomicity rule is explicit: a parent and its children commit together or not at all, and a test covers a child arriving without its parent.

Recommend the option you believe is right and say why in the commit, but implement whichever the reconciled documents end up stating - do not let the code and the docs disagree, which is the exact failure this task exists to prevent.
